senses.gloss:
शोष, अस्, m. drying up, exsiccation, dryness;
pulmonary consumption; emaciation; intumescence,
(for शोथ.)
—शोष-सम्भव, अम्, n. the root
of long pepper.
—शोषापहा (˚ष-अप्˚), f. ‘re-
moving consumption,’ a kind of plant (= क्लीत-
नक).

शोष शोष, शोषन, शोषित, &c. See
under rt. शुष्.

शोषक, अस्, इका, अम्, drying up, exsiccating,
absorbing, absorbent.

शोषण, अस्, ई, अम्, drying up, draining; causing
to fade; (अस्), m. one of the arrows of Kāma-deva
(god of love); the plant Bignonia Indica; (अम्), n.
the act of drying up; absorption; exhaustion; suck-
ing up, suction; dry ginger.
शोषणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be dried up or absorbed.
शोषयितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be dried up, &c.

शोषित, अस्, आ, अम्, dried, dried up, desiccated,
absorbed, sucked up, exhausted, drained, emptied.

शोषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, drying up (often at the end of
comps.); (इणी), f. ether, one of the five Dhāraṇās.

शोशुचत् शोशुचत्, अत्, अती, अत् (fr. Intens.
of rt. 3. शुच्), Ved. shining very brightly, very
splendid.

शोशुचान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. shining very brightly,
very radiant, resplendent; [cf. शुशुचान.]

शोशुच्यमान शोशुच्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr.
Intens. of rt. 1. शुच्), sorrowing intensely, grieving
deeply.

शोशुभ्यमान शोशुभ्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr.
Intens. of rt. 1. शुभ्), shining very much, very
brilliant.

शोस् शोस् (?), ind. a particle of reproach
or contempt.

सोष्मन् सोष्मन् (स-उष्˚ or स-ऊष्˚), आ, आ,
अ, having heat, warm; (in grammar) having aspi-
ration, aspirated (said of the aspirated letters ख्, घ्,
छ्, झ्, ठ्, ढ्, थ्, ध्, फ्, भ्, also of the sibilants
and the letter ह्); (आ), m. an aspirated letter, aspi-
rate.
—सोष्म-ता, f. the state or condition of being
aspirated, aspiration.
—सोष्म-वत्, आन्, m. ‘having
an aspirate,’ an aspirated word or syllable.
